findings.text: Upheld as a defect (Q6, behaviour: errors swallowed where the neighbours throw). The doctor's projectFolders (checks.ts:589-598) is new in this item (diff.patch:811). It catches every readdirSync error and returns [], and it filters names with isDirectory, which is false on any error. resolve.ts's projectFolders now refuses the same disk through namesIn and kindAt. probes/doctor-unreadable-projects.md ran it: with knowledge/projects at mode 000 or 600, the check warns and names the folder when there is a database. With no database it reports 'ok: 1 repository' and leaves the project out with no warning. That also contradicts ADR 0024:88 and CLAUDE.md:22 ('under the same guards'). Nothing is written. Fix: use namesIn and kindAt here, as resolve.ts:113-118 does.

Upheld as advisory (Q2/Q5). isDirectory and existsOnDisk are kindAt with every error read as 'no', and they remain at resolve.ts:209, repo.ts:972, 198/186-188, 574, 825 and checks.ts:583/723/734. The reviewer found no reachable path past an earlier refusal, so each depends on ordering. This is not a behaviour defect today.

Upheld as advisory (Q2). The .git walk keeps its own copy of unseen's rule, with a different set of 'not there' errnos (ENOENT only, against ENOENT and ENOTDIR) and a different message. Both fail closed.
Upheld as advisory (Q3/Q9). unseen advises 'check the permissions' for EIO, ELOOP, EMFILE and the like. The errno is now named, so this is the advice, not a hidden cause. The name could be sharper.

Upheld as advisory, carried. objects/ subfolders are not walked, and configArgs sets neither gc.auto=0 nor maintenance.auto=false. probes/auto-gc.md did not reproduce a detached gc. This is hardening outside the named risk areas.

Upheld as advisory under this rubric. The doctor's hand listing reads an unlistable folder as empty. That is a misreport with no write and no exposure of personal data. The same line is a code-quality defect.

Upheld as advisory, carried. A leftover lock stops inEachRepo, and a dropped intent record is read with no cap. Availability only.

Upheld as a defect (Q1: a failure with no way to see it; Q3: an irreversible delete). Line 594 (diff.patch:2366) deletes a repository's knowledge_repos, entry and proposal rows whenever its path is not 'folder', which covers 'other' (a link or a file) as well as 'absent'. resolve.ts:118 skips such a path, so rebuild neither refuses nor reports it. probes/link-at-project-repository.md ran both cases for a path-only project. Rebuild returned with 0 refused and the project's row and its two entry rows gone. With the folder put back, the row never returned and openRepo gave null. A write with the link or file in place was accepted into a new <name>-2 repository, with nothing said. This contradicts ADR 0024:85/88. Fix: delete only on 'absent'; refuse and name 'other' in projectFolders and in the loop.
Upheld as advisory (Q1). The refusal of an unreadable folder fails closed and clears on a rerun. It is code invalid, so no log line is written, and the hint names permissions even for EIO or EPERM.

Lowered from defect to advisory: no boundary crossed and no model reinterpreted. ADR 0010:18 decides that the Storage move carries only the database. It does not forbid locating the data directory elsewhere: ADR 0010:16 names the variables that do so. src/util/paths.ts:13-21 and the shim at plugin/wizardingcode-mem.sh:17-18 both honour WIZARDINGCODE_HOME, so the shims already follow it. The sentence is imprecise: WIZARDINGCODE_HOME moves the whole brand home, WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_DATA_DIR moves only this product, and either must be in every agent's environment. That is a wording drift, so it is advisory. Fix as the reviewer says, here and in the message at repo.ts:125.
Upheld as advisory, as filed. The doctor's hand copies read 'cannot look' as 'nothing there' while the module refuses. No boundary is crossed. The same line is a code-quality defect.

Upheld as advisory, as filed (Q1). listFolder and fingerprintOf (repo.ts:840) read an unlistable entries/ or proposals/ as empty, so rebuild drops that repository's derived rows. probes/unlistable-entries-folder.md confirms this at mode 000 and 300. The knowledge_repos row stays, and the rows come back from the untouched files at the next refresh. Recoverable, not data loss. It contradicts ADR 0024:88's wording (see architecture).
